jobs.full_offer_html:
Job Title

Senior Python Engineer (Barcelona-based / Relocation support to Barcelona)

Job Description

Senior Python Engineer, Billing & Accounts

Manychat builds AI-powered automations that help creators and brands engage with their audiences on Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and TikTok. We are 400+ people across three continents behind the leading platform for conversational growth.

As a Senior Python Engineer you will create the Python foundation for Manychat's Billing: payments, payment provider integrations, anti-fraud and local regulatory compliance, all tied to the pricing model every feature depends on. There is no roadmap yet, so you will design systems end to end, make the architectural decisions and experiment with what works best. Two mid-level engineers will join after you, and you will help them grow.

What you will do

  • Design and build Billing's Python foundation, where product features and the existing PHP backend work together.
  • Build async Python services for payments, payment provider integrations, invoicing, anti-fraud and regulatory compliance.
  • Design and integrate internal and third-party APIs with clear, stable contracts.
  • Build for failure: retries, idempotency, consistency and observability, so every payment is handled correctly.
  • Set the testing, CI/CD and rollout practices this layer runs on.
  • Mentor and set the technical bar for two mid-level engineers.
  • Work with cross-functional partners so your technical decisions fit how the business runs.

What we offer

  • Hybrid onboarding (start remotely) and relocation support for you and your family
  • Comprehensive health insurance for you and your family
  • Professional development budget for conferences, courses and learning resources
  • Flexible benefits package tailored to your priorities
  • Hybrid work and generous leave options
  • In-office perks, including free meals and snacks
  • Company-funded sports activities, annual offsites and team-building events

Manychat is an Equal Opportunity Employer. If you need an accommodation during the interview process, please indicate this in your application.

Restrictions

  • No telecommuting
  • No Agencies Please

Requirements

You need

  • 6+ years of commercial Python development in production, with Python as your primary language and recent hands-on work
  • Strong expertise in modern Python frameworks (FastAPI preferred; Django or Flask are fine)
  • Solid experience designing and integrating APIs, including third-party services
  • Strong understanding of async programming and concurrency (AsyncIO, non-blocking I/O)
  • Experience with PostgreSQL and large datasets
  • Experience building and maintaining backend systems under production load
  • Strong testing practices (unit and integration tests; PyTest preferred), CI/CD pipelines and Docker
  • Strong engineering judgment: you design systems end to end and make architectural decisions on your own
  • Mentoring or leadership experience of any kind
  • Experience working in cross-functional teams, with clear communication

Nice to have

  • Experience with billing, invoicing or payment systems
  • Experience with PHP
  • A product mindset and scale-up experience
  • Experience with queues, NoSQL or analytical systems
  • Deep database experience, such as replication, partitioning, sharding or PL/pgSQL
  • Hands-on experience with AI tools in your engineering work

About the Company

Creating content that resonates is great, and turning that attention into growth is even better. That is what Manychat does.

Our AI-powered automations help creators and brands engage with their audiences on Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and TikTok: at the right moment, with the right message, and without the manual work.

We are 400+ people across three continents behind the leading platform for conversational growth, with AI skills shaping how we build, how we work and how we grow. Manychat runs under serious load every day, and our stack is built for speed and durability.

Contact Info

  • Contact: Yuliya Lurye
  • E-mail contact: [email protected]
  • Web: https://careers.manychat.com/

jobs.full_offer_html:
The Python Steering Council and the Python Software Foundation are looking to hire the next CPython Developer-in-Residence. The position is full-time and remote, and is open to applicants inside and outside the US.

Background

CPython, the reference implementation of Python, is developed and primarily maintained by volunteers. The Developer-in-Residence program builds on this by providing support for the volunteers, taking on projects that require sustained, long-term attention, and filling gaps in the volunteer coverage.

The Developer-in-Residence works to assist CPython maintainers and the Steering Council. Areas of responsibility include:

  • Overseeing the long-term health of the project
  • Supporting the project's volunteers
  • Investigating project priorities and their tasks going forward, and working on those priorities
  • Communicating with sponsors and the community
  • Securing funding for the Developer-in-Residence roles (in co-operation with PSF staff)
  • Managing the Deputy and Supporting Developers-in-Residence roles

As an externally funded role, the term for this position will initially be one year, with the possibility of extension based on renewed availability of funding.

Responsibilities

This role is largely self-directing, with continuing coordination with PSF staff, the Steering Council, and the other Developers-in-Residence.

  • Help maintain, improve, and stabilize the CPython code base, libraries, and test suite, as well as the pull request and issue queues
  • Help maintain and improve the project's continuous integration infrastructure and buildbot fleet
  • Co-ordinate and manage the team of Developers-in-Residence
  • Manage larger project efforts that require co-ordination between volunteers (e.g. the GitHub Issues migration)
  • Administer and moderate Core Team communication channels (discuss.python.org, Discord, the GitHub org)
  • Support the Python Security Response Team and the Release Managers in their respective duties
  • Support the Core Team and other volunteers contributing to CPython
  • Author your own bugfixes and features in CPython and related projects
  • Attend Steering Council meetings on a regular cadence (currently every two weeks) and communicate regularly with PSF staff
  • Advocate for the CPython project and its developers to potential sponsors
  • Represent the CPython project at regional Python conferences and events
  • Support mentorship and outreach in order to broaden the CPython Core Team
  • Provide transparency by proposing and fulfilling a public record as agreed with the Steering Council and PSF staff
  • Publish regular updates on the PSF blog throughout the year, informing the community on progress

Required skills and experience

  • Strong project management skills
  • Well-organized and detail-oriented
  • Excellent written and verbal communication
  • Experience contributing to the CPython project
  • Experience working with a mix of stakeholders: volunteers, staff, and sponsors
  • Ability to balance demands and priorities, and to work independently in a fully remote environment

Preferred experience

  • Experience as a maintainer of open source software projects
  • Experience mentoring and supporting new contributors
  • Experience managing or leading a team of developers

Existing CPython Core Team members are strongly preferred. Willingness to travel to PyCon US or other international events is a plus.

Details

Location: Remote. Candidates not residing in the US will be considered under a contractor arrangement, conditional on legal and regulatory eligibility. Regular collaboration with US time zones is required, and some recurring availability in US Eastern is necessary for check-ins and reporting.

Compensation: $70,000–$170,000 USD per year for US employees, or a comparable contractor rate for international candidates, based on qualifications, experience, and location. US employees are eligible for healthcare and other benefits; contractor engagements do not include benefits.

This position reports to the PSF Executive Director and collaborates with the Steering Council.

How to apply

Applications are open until November 19, 2026. Apply directly through the JazzHR page linked above. The PSF asks for responses to a few short questions rather than a cover letter; all questions are required. They also request your resume, your GitHub username, and links to your CPython contributions.

Please note: the PSF asks that you not use AI to answer the screening questions — they would like to hear directly from you, in your own words.

About the Python Software Foundation

The Python Software Foundation is a US 501(c)(3) non-profit corporation that holds the intellectual property rights behind the Python programming language. The PSF also runs the PyCon US conference annually, supports other Python conferences and workshops around the world, and funds Python-related development through its grants program.

The PSF believes that the future of open source must include everyone, and welcomes all job-seekers regardless of race, color, ethnicity, religion, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, physical appearance, body size, socio-economic, veteran, or disability status. See the PSF Code of Conduct for more.
